FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Calder Line Ferries Announces Independent Safety Review and Fleet Standdown

HARBORTON, Meridia — Calder Line Ferries today announced that it has suspended all sailings on the Calder Strait route and commissioned an independent safety review of its six remaining vessels, effective immediately.

The review will be led by Northmark Marine Assurance, an accredited inspection firm, and will cover generator maintenance intervals, backup power testing, and crew emergency drills. The company said the review's findings will be shared with the Meridian Maritime Authority and published in summary form.

"Our first obligation is to the families affected, and our second is to make certain this cannot happen again," said Reinard Holt, chief executive of Calder Line Ferries. "We are standing the fleet down until an independent team tells us it is safe to sail."

The company has established a family liaison office at the Harborton terminal and a dedicated line for passengers seeking refunds or travel assistance. Calder Line Ferries said it is cooperating fully with the authority's inquiry and has provided maintenance documentation covering the past five years.

Calder Line Ferries operates passenger and vehicle services across the Calder Strait and has carried approximately 1.4 million passengers annually since 2019. The company employs 340 people in Meridia.

Media contact: Sonja Preet, director of communications, Calder Line Ferries.
Further information about the review will be posted at https://example-ferries.test/safety-review as it becomes available.
